name: Pediatric parapatellar arthrotomy for the proximal tibia
aliases: pediatric lateral or medial parapatellar proximal-tibial arthrotomy
corridor: Incision from the inferior patellar pole to the tibial physis on either side of the patellar tendon, with a matching capsular cut that stays off the meniscus and physis

positioning.text: Position so either side of the patellar tendon, the inferior pole, and the tibial physis can be marked.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the inferior patellar pole, both borders of the patellar tendon, and the tibial physis.

incision.text: Start at the lower pole of the patella and extend to the tibial physis on the chosen side of the tendon. Lengthen the cut if more articular surface is needed.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the capsule in line with the skin.

deep_interval.text: Use retractors to see the fracture. Avoid sharp dissection around the meniscus. Do not strip periosteum or compress the physis.

layers.text: Skin, capsule beside the patellar tendon, then the joint and proximal tibial articular surface.

structures_at_risk.text: The meniscus, the tibial physis, and periosteum around the growth plate are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Sharp work around the meniscus is the articular danger zone. Physeal compression is the growth-plate danger zone.

retraction_hazards.text: Retract the capsule rather than cutting toward the meniscus.

exposure.text: Shows intra-articular, avulsion, and osteochondral flake fractures of the proximal tibia.

limitations.text: The window stops at the physis unless a planned extension is added for more articular view.

indications.text: Used for intra-articular fractures, avulsions, and flake osteochondral fractures.

closure.text: Repair the capsule with absorbable suture and close skin.

complications.text: Complications include meniscal injury and physeal arrest from stripping or compression.

procedure_applications.condition: An intra-articular, avulsion, or osteochondral flake fracture of the proximal tibia needs a limited parapatellar arthrotomy

questions.question: Where does the incision run?
questions.answer: From the inferior patellar pole to the tibial physis on either side of the patellar tendon.

questions.question: What must be avoided around the meniscus?
